claims.conditions: A person is available to answer questions and to approve a written design; the request is creative or underspecified work (a new feature, component or behaviour change) that the request does not already fully specify. The agent can write a design document into the workspace.
claims.rationale: The source orders the work as: lay out approaches in a message of their own and have the person pick, write a design document, 'Get their approval of that doc', then invoke the planning skill (lines 28-33). Questions are asked one at a time and only when the answer would change what gets built (lines 101-106). A block marked HARD-GATE says 'Nothing gets built until your human partner approves the design doc', where building includes product code, scaffolding, installing dependencies, creating projects and invoking an implementation skill (lines 269-274). The gate has 'Two exceptions': if the person opted out of the questions 'the skill is done and the gate goes with it', and 'A spike they said yes to may be built; it stays labeled throwaway' (lines 276-279). The convergence step is therefore owned by the person, including the choice to waive it. Further qualifications visible in the text: the agent itself judges whether 'Everything that matters is in the request' and may then skip the process (lines 17-24), so the gate depends on the agent's own estimate of what is missing; the builder check depends on a sibling prompt file and a subagent tool (lines 250-266). Plausible failure mode: in an unattended run nothing can approve the document and the run stalls at the gate. Falsified if a session that has loaded this text writes product code before a design approval when the person has neither opted out of the questions nor agreed to a labelled spike; qualified by how often the skip path is taken on requests a reviewer would call underspecified.
